column1: # wasm-todo-tracking-refs.tsv
# The set of issue references a WASM-TODO marker is permitted to cite.
# scripts/lint-wasm-todo-issue-ref.sh checks marker SYNTAX (the `(#NNN)` form).
# That is not enough on its own: a marker pointing at a closed issue -- or at a
# merged PR number, which is not a tracking artifact at all -- satisfies the
# syntax while tracking nothing. This file supplies the semantics the syntax
# check cannot, without requiring network access in CI.
# Format: <issue>\t<state>\t<verified-UTC-date>\t<short description>
# Rules:
#   - A marker citing a ref that is ABSENT from this file fails the lint.
#   - A marker citing a ref recorded here as CLOSED fails the lint.
#   - Only `open` rows permit a marker.
# Refreshing: re-verify each row's state against the tracker and update the
# date column. A row's `open` claim is an assertion made by whoever last
# verified it; it is evidence only as of that date. Staleness is bounded and
# visible here rather than being silently assumed by a syntax-only gate.
# NOTE: this file is intentionally EMPTY of open rows. Every ref currently
# cited in-tree (#1451, #1758, #1475, #2050) is dead -- see issue #2827. The
# rows below record that finding so the lint reports the real backlog instead
# of passing over it. Repointing those markers at live, specific issues is
# tracked by #2827 and requires triage decisions this file cannot make.
